news.title: Football: Barcelona duo left out of Spain squad with four changes from World Cup victory
news.lede: Spain manager Luis de la Fuente has called up four new players to his Spain squad that won the World Cup in July, as Barcelona duo Gavi and Joan Garcia were left out. Espanyol forward Roberto Fernandez and Inter Milan goalkeeper Josep Martinez have received their first call-ups. Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen returns to the squad after missing out on victory in the US in July. Fermin Lopez has also been selected by De la Fuente after injury prevented him from being part of the World Cup.

news.title: Brazil Unveils Eight Stadiums For 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Brazil is preparing to host the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, with eight stadiums selected for the tournament. Eight stadiums in Brazil have been selected to host matches at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, with all eight venues having previously hosted games during the 2014 FIFA Men’s World Cup. The tournament will take place from June 24 to July 25, 2027, and will mark the first time the FIFA Women’s World Cup is held in South America. The selected venues are the Estádio do Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro, Estádio Nacional in Brasília, Estádio Mineirão in Belo Horizonte, Arena Castelão in Fortaleza, Estádio Beira-Rio in Porto Alegre, Arena Itaquera in São Paulo, Arena Fonte Nova in Salvador and Arena de Pernambuco in Recife, FIFA announced on Friday.

news.title: Elijah Just: Will Swansea City midfielder's unlikely journey lead to Premier League?
news.lede: Elijah Just was linked with likes of Celtic and Rangers before joining Swansea in July. Elijah Just remembers getting up as a kid in the early hours of the morning to see New Zealand play at the World Cup and to watch Premier League football. Sixteen years after the All Whites went to South Africa 2010, Just fulfilled one boyhood dream this summer by starring for New Zealand as they returned to the World Cup. Now comes the challenge of reaching the Premier League.

news.title: Soccer-Alexander-Arnold returns to England squad as Tuchel makes 10 changes from World Cup

news.title: Thomas Tuchel drops Arsenal and Chelsea stars in first England squad since World Cup heartbreak
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel has named his first England squad since the 2026 World Cup (Photo: Getty) Thomas Tuchel has named his first England squad since the 2026 World Cup, with Arsenal and Chelsea stars among the surprise names left out. Chelsea captain Reece James has been a stalwart under Tuchel but the right-back has been dropped, with Real Madrid’s Trent Alexander-Arnold receiving a surprising recall to the national team. Arsenal winger Noni Madueke has also been omitted but there is a return for Cole Palmer, who was controversially left at home during the World Cup, following a brilliant start to the season. Several inexperienced players have also been called up for the four upcoming Nations League matches, including Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha.

news.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold's offer to Thomas Tuchel after England World Cup squad snub
news.lede: Trent Alexander-Arnold has told Thomas Tuchel that he's always available for selection for England. The first Three Lions squad of the season will be announced today (Friday, September 18) ahead of the Nations League later this month. The Real Madrid defender was among several high-profile omissions from England's World Cup squad this past summer after a difficult first season in Spain. Alexander-Arnold, 27, has yet to lay a marker down at the Santiago Bernabeu and has started just one league game this season under new manager Jose Mourinho.

news.title: Palmer and Alexander-Arnold recalled after England World Cup snub
